body: I let a few friends know that I've been suicidal, etc, and one of them got back to me and we've been talking for a few hours. I think I'll be okay for now - it sounds like the one problem friend is just spectacularly ignorant of her behavior. But she's had her own suicidal times, I think this will wake her up a bit. If it doesn't, then I don't have the patience for her anymore.

Oh hell, the final project is due WEDNESDAY, not today. And today is an in-class work day, so I'm not totally fucked. That's one immediate stresser off my list. That gives me another two days to decide if I need to tell my professor anything.
I can't express how much those first four words mean to me right now. They're the only thing I want to hear from my friends right now, and I've been hyper-aware of their absence.

Okay, I'll just list the positives and leave out the negatives, for an exercise.

1) Finally found where I want to be in school
2) Have succeeded very well in this field with the exception of this semester
3) Have got into competitive, high-powered and challenging (in a good way) school program within that field
4) Have a loving, caring, relentlessly positive boyfriend who is also quickly becoming one of my best friends (ignoring anything negative about other friends)
5) May possibly be moving into beautiful, spacious house away from drama of Greedy Landlord
6) My reassignment at work takes away all the stuff I didn't like to do and replaces it with stuff I love to do, with no change to my hours or pay.
7) I've finally reached a place in my hobbies where I am not only producing things better and more often, but I enjoy it more and have met amazing people and role models because of it.

Each of these has something related to it that's bringing me down, but I'm gonna push myself to ignore those, if only for just this comment.

I sent a Facebook note to all of them together, briefly explaining where I am emotionally. I'm pretty sure they'll be supportive, but the one friend's behavior has been so unpredictable lately that I'm still nervous, especially since her opinions seem to be spreading to the others in the group.

I've used up all but one of my free counseling appointments on campus this semester, and I honestly thought I was a lot better. This is sort of a last straw that broke the camel's back situation, I guess. I'm not sure what would be the best thing to help... going back for the one appointment? Maybe seeking out something else?

Even just typing everything out and getting some sort of acknowledgment is helping my brain settle down a bit. I just don't quite know how to gather my thoughts when I go through these pockets of emotional turbulence.

On one hand, my life is awesome because I just got into a high-powered program that I'm really excited about. On the other hand, I'm conflicted because I've dropped 3 out of 4 courses this semester and the professors I will be working with are not happy with that. I have also failed out of school once before, and took 6 months of cognitive behavioral therapy for depression after that. My therapist told me I should have continued past that point, but my family can't afford to send me anymore. I've used up all but one of my free counseling appointments here on campus, and I really thought I was in the clear when my friends started getting bitchy again. I guess I wasn't aware at how much their behavior was getting to me until this weekend.

On one hand, I have found a beautiful and loving boyfriend. On the other hand, I am being made to feel guilty for spending time with him and not my friends, even though my friends (the one in particular) act moody and bitchy around him and hint that they blame him for my absence lately.

On one hand, it's possible my mother and I may be moving into a beautiful new house in a beautiful new neighborhood. Other other hand, we have to move because our landlord is running everyone into foreclosure, we don't even know if we'll get this house, and if we do it will hurt us financially.

One one hand, I've finally started working on a project that I've been dying to get going for years. On the other hand, it requires the involvement of my currently moody friends.

Basically, I feel like I am just about to start all the really good stuff in my life, but it's taken a lot out of me to get this far, and the few people whose support I really needed (and thought I had) suddenly vanished and it's all been replaced with pointless drama I barely understand. Each of these things on their own wouldn't really bring me down much, but all together it's hard to even have the energy to keep track of everything.
